body:
Found while working #321. Two findings, both beyond what that issue describes.

## 1. The worst collapses are duplicates, not just mis-mappings

`CoCl2 x 6 H2O` sits on the **anhydrous** term `CHEBI:35696` — while a sibling
record already holds the correct one:

```
CHEBI:35696  CoCl2 x 6 H2O                     <- anhydrous term
CHEBI:53503  Cobalt chloride hexahydrate       occ=123, CAS 7791-13-1, correct
```

Same for nickel: `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` on `CHEBI:34887` while
`Nickel (II) chloride hexahydrate` (occ=122) correctly holds `CHEBI:53542`.

This is the `Ca-pantothenate` shape from #315 — a notation the merge pass does
not recognise as naming the same substance (`Ca-` vs `Calcium …`, here
`CoCl2 x 6 H2O` vs `Cobalt chloride hexahydrate`). Having escaped the merge, the
survivor was then grounded to the nearest thing lexical matching could find: the
anhydrous parent.

So the remedy for those two is a **merge**, not a promotion — and a promotion
would have failed anyway, because the target identifier is already taken.
Worth adding formula-notation ↔ spelled-out equivalence to the duplicate
normaliser, alongside the `Ca-`/`Na-` prefix expansion #315 suggested.

## 2. CAS numbers are scrambled within each hydrate family

Independently of the mapping, the `cas_rn` values are close to arbitrary:

```
CoCl2, CoCl2 x 2 H2O, x 4 H2O, x 6 H2O   ALL carry 7646-79-9  (the anhydrous CAS)
NiCl2 x 2 H2O, NiCl2 x 5 H2O             both carry 7791-20-0 (the HEXAhydrate CAS)
NiCl2 x 6 H2O                            carries 7718-54-9    (the anhydrous CAS)
Na2HPO4 x 2 H2O                          carries 7558-79-4    (anhydrous; the dihydrate is 10028-24-7)
Na2HPO4 x 3/6/7/12 H2O                   all carry 7782-85-6
```

ChEBI's own xrefs give the right values — `CHEBI:91258` (dihydrate) →
`cas:10028-24-7`, `CHEBI:53542` (nickel hexahydrate) → `cas:7791-20-0` — so the
correct CAS for a hydrate is recoverable wherever a specific term exists.

Note the interaction: `7791-20-0` is *currently* on the di- and pentahydrate
records and *belongs* to the hexahydrate. Any CAS-keyed dedup or join run today
would merge the wrong records.

## Scope

`#321`'s 39 records include 4 terms absorbing 13 records. Of those 13, ChEBI has
a specific term for exactly 4:

| record | target | action |
|---|---|---|
| `Na2HPO4 x 2 H2O` | CHEBI:91258 | promote (free) |
| `Na2HPO4 x 12 H2O` | CHEBI:91259 | promote (free) |
| `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` | CHEBI:53503 | **merge** (taken) |
| `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` | CHEBI:53542 | **merge** (taken) |

The remaining 9 (`Na2HPO4 x 3/6/7`, `CoCl2 x 2/4`, `NiCl2 x 2/5`, `FeCl2 x 6/7`)
have no ChEBI term and no trustworthy CAS, so they need §3 step 2 with a
*verified* CAS or step 3, per record. Not attempted blind.

comments.body:
A cheap normalisation finds these mechanically. Normalising hydrate notation before comparing labels — expand `dihydrate`/`hexahydrate`/… to `x N H2O`, treat `·` as ` x `, collapse `Na2-` to `Na2`, then strip non-alphanumerics — yields **10 collisions across the live corpus, every one holding two different identifiers**:

| normalised | records |
|---|---|
| `dtagatose` | `D-(-)-tagatose` = CHEBI:4249 · `D-tagatose` = CHEBI:16443 |
| `feso4x7h2o` | `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` = CHEBI:75836 · `FeSO4 x 7H2O` = CHEBI:75832 |
| `glucose` | `Glucose` = CHEBI:17234 · `glucose` = CHEBI:42758 |
| `maltose` | `Maltose` = CHEBI:17306 · `maltose` = CHEBI:18167 |
| `methylbetadxylopyranoside` | `methyl-beta-D-xylopyranoside` = cas:0612-05-5 · `Methyl Beta-D-xylopyranoside` = CHEBI:74863 |
| `mgcl2x6h2o` | `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` = CHEBI:86345 · `MgCl2x 6 H2O` = CHEBI:6636 |
| `mgso4x7h2o` | `MgSO4·7H2O` = CHEBI:32599 · `MgSO4 x 7 H2O` = CHEBI:31795 |
| `nacetylmuramicacid` | `N-acetylmuramic acid` = CHEBI:47965 · `n-Acetyl-muramic acid` = CHEBI:47966 |
| `na2seo3x5h2o` | `Na2SeO3·5H2O` = CHEBI:48843 · `Na2SeO3 x 5 H2O` = CHEBI:131361 |
| `quinicacid` | `Quinic acid` = CHEBI:26493 · `(-)-quinic Acid` = CHEBI:17521 |

Note the pairs are not merely cosmetic — in each case the two records land on **different ChEBI terms**, so the split is already propagating downstream. `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` vs `MgCl2x 6 H2O` (one missing space) resolve to the hexahydrate and the *anhydrous* term respectively, which is this issue's thesis in one line.

## Four already fixed

The same normalisation, applied during the review of #341, caught four hydrates that PR had just minted `kgmicrobe.compound:` identifiers for while a correctly-mapped sibling already held the specific ChEBI term:

    Na2-EDTA x 2 H2O          -> CHEBI:64758, held by `Na2EDTA·2H2O`
    Na2MoO4·2H2O              -> CHEBI:75213, held by `Na2MoO4 x 2 H2O`
    Sodium acetate·3H2O       -> CHEBI:32138, held by `Sodium acetate trihydrate`
    Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O -> CHEBI:32142, held by `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O`

Those are merged in #341 (`a23d8d9b`). The 10 above are the residue and are **not** addressed there.

## Suggestion

This normalisation is cheap enough to run as a check. `audit_duplicate_identifiers` already reports the inverse defect ("same name, different identifiers") but treats it as ungated commentary, and it compares raw names, so it misses `MgSO4·7H2O` vs `MgSO4 x 7 H2O` entirely. Folding hydrate-notation normalisation into that check would gate the class that keeps producing these.

title: Hydrate collapse is partly a duplicate problem: formula-notation labels shadow correctly-mapped siblings
